newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Former Venezuelan leader appeals fine.
newsitem.headline: Former Venezuelan leader appeals fine.

text.p: Lawyers representing former Venezuelan President Carlos Andres Perez and four of his top aides introduced an appeal on Wednesday against a $603,295 fine imposed by the Supreme Court for the misuse of public funds.
The lawyers told reporters the fine, announced by the Supreme Court on Tuesday, was baseless and would be vigorously challenged. "We have a series of objections," attorney Alberto Arteaga said.
Perez served a 28-month sentence under house arrest after being found guilty of misappropriating $17 million from a secret security spending account.
The conviction in May 1996 made Perez, 73, the first Latin American leader to be convicted of corruption, two years after the charges forced him out of office.
The former leader maintained his innocence and launched a new political movement after completing his term in September 1996.
